ROM FINDINGS (each reproduced on the ROM's own code, each as the reviews and the fix pass corrected it; 1–8
evnt_multi's, 9–20 the dispatcher's):
1. **THE BUTTONS evnt_multi ANSWERS ARE STALE UNLESS A BUTTON EVENT CAME** (wave 0's finding 4 and wave 1's 3, from
   ev_multi's side, pinned). ev_rets runs BEFORE the aprets (`$fe6ba8` against `$fe6bce`) and hands out `$c792`, the
   high word of the last answer apret took IN AN EARLIER CALL; ev_multi stores the real buttons over it only when NO
   button event was asked for (`$fe6baa btst #1,d7`), and apret's own word only when the button event CAME. ON THE
   SNAPSHOT'S OWN MACHINE, nothing staged: the call the screen manager's own code makes (`ev_multi(KEYBD + BUTTON +
   M1, $96d8, $96d8, 0, $0001ff01, 0, answers)`, `$fe49f4`) — M1 comes, **buttons = 216**, the width of the menu bar's
   active rectangle, no button down. After a mouse wait for a 20-wide rectangle: 20. And made by the twin itself: a
   woken mouse wait's apret leaves the rectangle's WIDTH in `$c792`, and with a press and a rectangle come in ONE wake
   the buttons answered are the button's (read after the buttons' apret, before the rectangle's overwrites the word).
2. **A call that asks for NO event blocks for good**: nothing is queued, mwait is handed 0, and "none of them come" is
   true — the process is left WAITING with no wait, which no event ends. So does a flags word with only bits above the
   six. (Pinned at dsptch.)
3. **A RETURNING evnt_multi LEAVES A STACK ADDRESS IN A FREED EVB**: the message wait is queued over a QPB in
   ev_multi's own frame (`-8(a6)`); when another event ends the call, acancel frees that EVB as it is — EVB_PARM still
   the frame's address until get_evb's bfill next clears it. Harmless in the ROM (nothing reads a free EVB's
   parameter); BY NATURE another longword on each shore — dropped by name and vetted (both name the same QPB), at a
   return as where the wait parks.
4. **The fast path's button test looks in the click record FIRST when more than one change was posted since the last
   ev_rets** (`$c836 > 1`, signed): a press AND its release that both came while the process was busy still answer a
   wait for the button DOWN — with the buttons before the release and the record's clicks. With exactly ONE change the
   record is not tried: a press, the button wanted UP, blocks though the buttons before the press were up. Where the
   record's buttons AND the buttons as they are would both answer (the left held, the right clicked: two changes), the
   record's answer alone: buttons = 3, not 1.
5. **The key queue the fast path reads is `rlr`'s own (its PD's CDA); akbin's, a moment later, is `gl_cda`'s**
   (`$fe69d2` against `$fe5524`). The two are one on every machine the scheduler makes; pinned apart by a poked
   `gl_cda`.
6. **An event bit come that no wait holds is answered as A KEY OF 100** (a poked PD_EVFLG — no run leaves one): the
   new wait takes the bit, mwait finds it come, acancel cancels the wait (it is not completed), and apret, asked for
   an event no EVB holds, answers `APRET_NO_EVB` — which ev_multi stores as the key. A road to apret's "unreachable"
   100 arm (wave 0).
7. **Past the last EVB the waits are built at address 0** — the divergence above (argument-class only; "two
   accessories are enough" was wrong).
8. Smaller, each pinned: the timer is tested before the message on the fast path and queued after it (the fast path's
   order is UNOBSERVABLE: the timer arm stores nothing); a timer of 1 ms is not "no time" and blocks; an event bit is
   the WAIT's, not the flag's (a message and a timer alone wait on bits 1 and 2); a cancelled double-click wait stays
   counted in `$c84e`; the answers' pointer is re-read and put on the bus for every store; `$97fe` is cleared only
   when a message CAME; the fast path with HALF a message in the pipe (index 1..15) does not end in the ROM — the C
   reaches the pipes' named refusal.
9. **The Line-F handler leaves ITS OWN D1 and D2 in every saved context.** savestate is entered through it, so a
   process's UDA holds D1 = `$7c8` (savestate's call-word offset) and D2 = the SR at disp's call — and a resumed
   process is handed those back. Under our `jsr` the caller's own D1/D2 are saved: the switch keeps D2 for a C caller.
10. **disp's argument slot lies ABOVE the dispatcher's stack.** After savestate's `lea $8c1a,sp`, disp's `move.l
    a5,(sp)` stores at `$8c1a..$8c1d` — the longword AT the stack's top: the PD it queues, last the UDA it enters. The
    map's "dispatcher stack" ends below it.
11. **gotopgm parks the SR in spl's save word** (`$8996`), not one of its own.
12. **disp_act of a process already last links it to itself** (`move.l a4,(a5)` then `move.l a5,(a3)` with a3 = a5).
13. **Two processes woken in one forker pass are entered in the woken list's order** (drl is drained head first,
    each appended to rlr's tail): a delay run out and the mouse on the bar → the desk, then the screen manager.
    (CORRECTED by band 4 wave 3: this said "in the order they were woken". The list is filled at its HEAD, so its
    order is LAST WOKEN FIRST — wave 3's finding 1, pinned by a key that wakes the desk after a press woke the
    screen manager.)
14. **The ROM's dispatcher uses 188 of its 640 bytes whatever is queued** — Alcyon's frames under forker are shallower
    than the VDI call the keyboard poll makes. (OURS go deeper under forker than under the poll: 300 / 312 measured,
    356 by the listing.)
15. **An interrupt taken inside the dispatcher needs up to 240 bytes of its stack**, not an exception frame and a
    `movem`: the ROM's own Timer C handler goes 140 bytes down the INTERRUPTED stack on the tick that reaches
    etv_timer (the AES's tick glue `jsr`s the routine it displaced AFTER putting the interrupted SP back, `$fed46e`),
    the ACIA's 140 on a mouse packet's last byte, and a vertical blank that redraws the cursor 100 — with an MFP
    interrupt (level 6) nested on the blank (level 4). (OUR OWN entries need 192 / 188 / 152 — 344 nested: the risk
    block under the Components table.)
16. **The glue's private stacks are 92 and 96 bytes**, the ROM's deepest use 70 (a release queued at once: b_click's
    Line-F call of forkq), 54 and 42. Overflow would land, in order, on the tick's countdown `$9492`, its elapsed
    count `$948e`, the chained tick vector `$948a`, then the two parked stack pointers. No nesting: both glues run
    inside MFP interrupts at IPL 6 and nothing under them lowers the mask.
17. **forker's recorder copies a queue entry code and all** (`$fe4c8e`, eight bytes) and merges ticks BY COMPARING
    CODE ADDRESSES (the record before the cursor against tchange's own): fork codes live in appl_trecord's buffer.
18. **`$c908`, the word after the fork queue's count, is live data** (the control manager's saved cursor count): the
    count is tested as a WORD (`tst.w $c906`, `$fe4d94`; disp's `tst.w`), and a long read would be nonzero with an
    empty queue whenever the screen manager holds a mouse it found shown.
19. **disp puts a process whose status is neither 0 nor 1 on NO list** (`$fe4dd8` falls through): nothing can wake it.
    No routine stores such a status.
20. Dead code: disp's `LF_RET` (`$fe4e00`); savestate's guarded arm; `$fe395c`. And one of the BUILD: GCC calls a twin
    it calls twice THROUGH A REGISTER (`lea aes_ev_multi,%a5` / `jsr (%a5)`) — an arrival like any `jsr`'s; the
    two-blob pin accepts the load and refuses a jump through the register.

**aes — band 4 wave 3 (the rows that switch: the foundation, the slices W, M, U, their review's fix pass, and the
steps S — the sessions that switch — and T — the event tape, ap_trecd and ap_tplay): what is unpinned or owed, what
the wave's step R still holds, what this wave supersedes above, and the ROM's findings.**

NOT RECONSTRUCTED BY STEP T, AND REFUSED BY NAME: **appl_tplay at a scale of 0.** The ROM divides a timer record's
milliseconds by zero inside the Alcyon runtime's ldiv (`divs.w`); the 68000 takes vector 5 — an `rte` on this machine —
and the ROM's playback carries on with whatever the divide left, and returns. ldiv's C core halts at that divide by
name (`src/aes/strings.c`: "not reconstructed: divs.w by zero"), and so does the C's playback: refused, never answered
with a quotient of our own making (`test_a_scale_of_0_is_the_runtime_s_divide_by_zero_which_the_c_refuses_by_name`).
A playback with no timer record never divides and plays at any scale.

UNPINNED / OWED, by name, each with its reason:
- **idle moving ONE woken process a turn** (a mutant of `evdisp.c`) WAS unpinned on a blob (no row woke two
  processes in one idle) and IS HELD since the fix pass: ev_multi's row "a key and the mouse onto the bar in one
  idle" wakes the screen manager and the desk together, and the mutant leaves the manager on the woken list where
  the call returns — the image differs on the host's model and on both blobs.
- **TWO FOREIGN WINDOWS INSIDE ONE DOOR CALL ARE UNREACHABLE, NOT OWED** (restated by step S; held on STAND-IN
  COUNTERS alone, `test_windows_accumulate_between_two_calls_and_inside_one`). The reason: a rebound entry has TWO
  dispatch sites — mwait's and a yield — and each is passed AT MOST ONCE A CALL; a window ends only where the row's
  process is resumed, so however many turns other processes take while it is parked they are ONE window (fs_input's
  slice: the screen manager entered three times, one window). A second window in the same call would need the call
  to park twice, and no entry does. **TWO BETWEEN THE SAME TWO DOOR CALLS** is reachable in principle since step T —
  ap_tplay dispatches OUTSIDE any rebound entry, a bare yield a record — and reached by no registered row: its one
  row with another process's turn has one window. Stand-in counters hold the arithmetic. Two windows in one RUN, each inside
  another call, ARE a registered row (mn_do, the desk's turn in two of its waits).
- **THREE TAIL MUTANTS OF THE WAITS ARE HELD ON THE ROWS THAT SWITCH BY CYCLE PINS ALONE** — their behaviour is
  killed only by the old leaf batteries (staged machines, at dsptch) and, where said, by nothing on a blob:
  ev_mesag clearing the sent mark AFTER its read (the menu chain never sets the mark: a staged mark is what shows
  it), mwait_act with no "arrived" arm (unreachable in a real run: finding 7), and — until the row above — idle
  moving one woken process a turn. A pin says the code MOVED; it does not say what it did. (The slice's sweep
  printed "0" for this split everywhere: its classifier's pattern never matched. Re-run and re-read in the fix
  pass.)
- **ev_mesag's sent-mark order in a woken run**: the menu chain's message never sets the mark (`AES_CTL_MESSAGE_SENT`,
  `$97fe`), so the tail's clear is seen only over a staged mark. It needs a wake by the control manager's own window
  message.
- **A bare dsptch yield INTO ANOTHER PROCESS as a registered row**: CLOSED by step T — ap_tplay "the mouse played
  onto the menu bar and off it: the screen manager entered from a yield" (the move run by our forker under the
  second yield, the third yield entering the manager: one foreign window). No change of the watch was needed.
- **fm_alert's two ends-blocked cases**: CLOSED by step S — both are rows that switch (a click while the alert waits
  answers it). **fs_input's ends-blocked sessions** (20; this list said 21): CLOSED at Tier 1 — each goes on through
  its wake to DONE — and two sessions the user is waited for in are PRICED BY THEIR SLICES (a slice's marks are per
  process now). The twenty themselves are NOT PRICED: each is woken by Return (one by the button let go, then
  Return) with no other process running — the shape the priced session "the user waited for at each wait" prices.
- **A RECORDING WITH ANOTHER PROCESS'S TURN INSIDE IT IS RED ON A BLOB** (step T; Tier 1 green; RULING: Tier 1 only
  for now). The events delivered inside the foreign window are run — and RECORDED — by the ROM's forker on both
  shores (the window is the ROM's code), so on a blob the buffer holds the ROM's fork-function addresses where our
  ap_trecd looks for our own entries, and numbers them 0 (a timer's) where the ROM's numbers them 2 (a mouse's):
  two bytes. The registry relocates a recording where a run begins and ends and where a delivery is laid, not where
  a window closes. Held as a refusal by name (`test_a_recording_across_another_process_s_turn_is_refused_on_a_blob`),
  registered nowhere. It goes with band 5 (ctlmgr in C: no foreign forker).
- **A played scale that makes a timer record's wait fall below −1 tick never wakes** (step T's finding on the ROM's
  run; no case holds it — a negative scale's row waits "no tick"). **More than 4,095 records** (ap_trecd's count is
  a signed WORD divide of the cursor's distance): PINNED AT TIER 1 since gate 13 — "out of the buffer band's reach"
  was false (finding 21 below); no blob runs it (ten seconds a ROM run). **ap_trecd's D0 high word**: the ROM's is
  pinned (`$00fe`, or 0 where no record was numbered); OURS IS NOT COMPARED — a word answer, two bytes on the bench,
  `d0.w` at its callers. **ap_tplay reads a record byte-wise off the bus** where the ROM calls lbcopy into a frame local: ACCEPTED
  by ruling (the same bytes on every machine; an odd buffer is a row of the labelled class).
- **THREE TAPE MUTANTS ARE HELD BY CYCLE PINS ALONE** (five in the author's sweep, "equivalent on every reachable
  machine"; gate 13 RAN the two that are not — the records counted unsigned, the distance not cut to a word: each
  answers `$100e` for the ROM's `$f00e` past 32,767 bytes — and both die by behaviour now). The three left, each
  with what would show it and why this harness cannot make it: ap_tplay not clearing the playing flag at its start
  (0 wherever ONE caller begins; A SECOND PROCESS calling appl_tplay while another is mid-playback after a mouse
  record finds it 1 — the staged application's stub pushes one immediate and ap_tplay takes three arguments);
  ap_trecd not clearing the recorder's flag after its loop (the loop ends on the flag being 0; a second caller of
  appl_trecord arming it in between would differ), and a do-while in place of its while (the flag was set a moment
  before, under the mask; the recorder stops itself only where forker runs). NO ROM-MADE MACHINE OF THIS HARNESS,
  and not "equivalent": each differs with a second caller. A pin says the code MOVED; it does not say what it did.
- **The blocked cases NO wake reaches**: wm_update / fm_own after an unbalanced release, ap_sendmsg to the sender's
  own full pipe. Held where they block (the image at dsptch), and nothing after. THE WAITS' OWN SUCH CASES ARE A
  TABLE (`evlib.NOT_WOKEN`: 11 scenarios, 30 blocked arrivals — 12 and 31 while one of them was wrongly in it)
  HELD BY A SWEEP since the fix pass: every kind of interrupt there is, each alone at the dispatcher's first
  idle, over every one of the 30 on the ROM's own run — none returns in its caller (`evlib.what_wakes`; the sweep
  shown non-vacuous on a wait of each kind an interrupt satisfies). THE SCREEN MANAGER'S WAIT TO ENTER A RECTANGLE
  stood in that table, "tried" with a move OUT of the rectangle: the move INTO it wakes it, and it is a registered
  row now (mwait's third, the row's process the screen manager). Where the wait is ANOTHER PROCESS's to satisfy
  (a pipe's other end, a lock's holder: five entries, nothing "tried") the sweep is what says no interrupt does it
  instead; that no PROCESS does is each entry's stated reason — the waiter is the pipe's only reader, the only
  ROM-run writer writes to the desk, the lock's holder is parked by a harness call or is nobody — and is held by
  nothing further. SINCE STEP S BOTH HALVES ARE HELD: the sweep takes CHAINS too (`evlib.EVERY_CHAIN`, 14: what one
  interrupt alone cannot bring — the menu chain, ticks at four successive idles, each kind of event after the
  mouse went onto the bar or off it, a key, a click and the ticks at the poll between two processes' turns) and is
  held to wake EVERY arrival a registered wake wakes (it had answered nothing for sixteen of them); and each of
  the five reasons is a FACT READ OFF THE ROM-MADE MACHINE at every arrival of its scenario
  (`evlib.ONLY_ANOTHER_PROCESS`: the pipe full and the caller's own with no reader waiting, the pipe empty with no
  writer waiting, the lock held by a process that is PARKED, or counted to −1 with no owner), each shown false of a
  machine it does not describe. STILL A SWEEP, NOT A PROOF: 12 interrupts and 14 chains are the members somebody
  thought of. AND TWO OF THE ELEVEN ARE NOT "CANNOT BE WOKEN" (gate 13): `wind_update(BEG), the lock another's` and
  the staged application's `a second process queues on the lock` hold the lock in A HARNESS-PARKED PROCESS — the
  desk, parked FOR A KEY — and a single Return at the first idle un-parks THAT HOLDER, whose continuation is the
  run's sentinel: the run ends "in another process" and THE WAITER'S TAIL IS NOT RUN. That is an UNPINNED TAIL on
  those two machines, which `what_wakes` — it keeps only returns in the caller — had answered as silence. Held
  now: the sweep's every answer is pinned (`evlib.swept`; `test_no_interrupt_wakes_a_wait_said_never_to_be_woken`:
  "idles for ever" but three members that end those four arrivals in the holder — Return alone and after either
  opener — and the staged timers' five that end in the application), the three chains "at the poll after it" are
  NOT TAKEN on those four arrivals and are counted as NO EVIDENCE (23 members answer there, not 26), and the fact
  reads WHAT THE HOLDER ITSELF WAITS FOR (`_a_lock_whose_holder_is_parked_for_a_key`, false of the screen manager's
  menu holding the lock). THE TAIL ITSELF IS RUN OVER A ROM-RUN HOLDER: a new scenario, `wind_update(BEG), the lock
  the screen manager's menu holds` (`evlib.THE_LOCK_THE_MENU_HOLDS`), whose two blocked arrivals — ev_block's and
  mwait's — are woken by the menu let go and taken on to their return at Tier 1 (64 woken arrivals, 62 before;
  ev_block's is the registered row "a wait for the lock the screen manager's menu holds").
- **`sr_drops` on INTERRUPTED rows**: the registrar still reads the save words by memory change, not by the write
  ledger — loud (a byte that changes and is not dropped reds), never silent.
- **`aes_event.qpb_addresses_kept` reads the QPB where the run ends**, which finding 4 shows is too late for ev_mesag.
  Harmless for today's direct rows (their parked QPB is ap_rdwr's own frame, still live at dsptch); the rows that
  switch read it while its frame is live (`aes_switching`).
- **`refused_where_the_rom_blocks`** had no caller left in any routine's battery (fs_input's two went with step S:
  `blocked_then_woken`); RETIRED BY STEP R — its six own-tests are spelt on `interrupted` ending blocked, each
  assertion kept.
- **Two registrar mutants survived in the author's logs with no argument on record; each has one now.** `q2b` — an
  unseen QPB address "settled as none": EQUIVALENT BY THE LINE BEFORE IT (`aes_switching._qpbs_left` refuses a
  non-empty `unseen` by name; the mutant's filter can only drop an address `unseen` holds, so it never drops one).
  `q16` — a QPB seen (or not) at the ROM's idle INSIDE A FOREIGN WINDOW: EQUIVALENT BY WHERE A WAIT IS QUEUED — the
  row's process queues its wait before it blocks, so its QPB is seen at our own first idle or, where the dispatch
  finds another process ready and never idles, where it is resumed; inside a window the row's process stands
  parked and queues nothing, so a sighting there can only repeat one (re-made in the fix pass as "no QPB seen at an
  idle inside a foreign window": survives, as argued; the author's own text of it was not kept).
- **Accepted as equivalent**: ev_multi's known pair (mwait's or acancel's answer thrown away singly), and a
  window's glue left in an open call's glue. **NO LONGER AMONG THEM: idle polling the keyboard AFTER it moves the
  woken** (`t13`). The two statements commute in every image, which is why no compare saw it — but the POINT IN
  ITS LOOP at which the dispatcher polls is observable the moment an interrupt arrives there: a delivery at a poll
  that is no idle is checked against which process stands woken and which ready (`aes_switch.what_idle_tests`),
  and the mutant is refused on both blobs where the key would be laid (the fifth pilot, and ev_multi's row of the
  same poll). On the HOST it still survives, by nature: the model's poll hook is called where the C says it
  polls, a line above both statements.
- **The message's apret BEFORE the rectangles'** (`j09` — a message AND a rectangle in one wake) is STILL UNPINNED:
  both writer rows that ask a rectangle too answer the message alone (the mouse is the writer's while its menu is
  down). A delivery at a poll does not reach it either: the rectangle's wait is posted by mchange for the mouse's
  OWNER, and the owner is the screen manager until its menu is up — after the desk has run.
- **The host slots stay ONE FRAME FOR EVERY PROCESS** but the two QPBs': the audit
  (`test_aes_event.SLOTS_HELD_WHERE_PARKED`) finds it sound while one C process can be inside a routine, and band 5
  (ctlmgr in C, calling mn_do while the desk sits in fm_do or a drag) owes each of them `HOST_PROCESSES` frames.
  NEWLY AUDITED BY STEP S as held across a wait: `AES_FS_INPUT_FRAME` (with fm_do's under it) and
  `AES_FM_ALERT_FRAME` (with fm_do's, the watch's and fm_button's) — the same debt.
- **STILL THE ROM'S ON BOTH SHORES, by the provisional pricing rule**: another process's turn and the dispatch that
  hands the machine back after it (the foreign window). After a foreign turn only the PARKING is our dispatcher's.

SUPERSEDED BY THIS WAVE, in the paragraphs above — each describes the tree as it was then: band 3 wave 0's "UNPINNED:
gr_watchbox's 0 answer" (pinned by its row blocked three times); band 4 wave 1's "Nothing after a switch … Wave 3"
(mwait's return, ev_block's apret after a block, unsync's continuation and the non-zero answers run across a real
switch on both blobs) and "ev_timer has no Tier 3 row, by nature" (four rows); band 4 wave 2's "THE TARGET BUILD'S
FRAME ACROSS A REAL SWITCH" (every row that switches; but its "The message's apret BEFORE the rectangles'" STANDS —
the real menu chain does not reach it either), "EVERY HOST SLOT A ROUTINE HOLDS ACROSS A WAIT … the audit is wave 3's" (made, above) and "FLIP 3's known
debts" (**Next** has them as they stand: `$fcff0a`'s trap-frame half is pinned by step T); the foundation's "NOT
BUILT" list WHOLE (its first item, a sliced session that switches, is step S's); band 4 wave 2's "OWED BY ROUTINES NOT
RECONSTRUCTED YET" table in its last row (appl_tplay's two justretf sites: ported by step T) and its sentence on a
recording made under the ROM (corrected in place).

ROM FINDINGS (each on the ROM's own run; 1–7 and 9–21 pinned by a case, 8 recorded only; 10–16 are step T's, the
event tape's, 17–18 step S's, and 19–21 gate 13's):
1. **The woken list is LAST IN, FIRST OUT, and a key that arrives in an idle is that idle's last fork.** A process
   woken is put at the HEAD of the woken list (`$fe3f5e` signal's and pstart's store), idle drains it head first
   onto the ready list's tail, and the dispatcher polls the keyboard after the interrupts have queued their forks.
   So a key typed IN THE IDLE the menu's press is taken at wakes the desk AFTER the press woke the screen manager,
   and THE DESK RUNS FIRST: it answers the key alone, its message wait cancelled, no message written yet. WHERE IT
   HOLDS: of the processes woken out of ONE idle's forks. It does NOT say that a key and a message never come in
   one wake (the slices wrote that, and a passing test pinned it: finding 9).
9. **idle polls the keyboard EVERY time round its loop — with a process woken or ready too — and a key that arrives
   there is polled before that process runs.** (`$fe4d70`; found by the wave's review, pinned by the fix pass.)
   Return taken at the poll AFTER the press's forks have run — nothing ready, the screen manager WOKEN, nothing
   queued — is posted to the desk's wait while the manager has yet to be moved: the desk is woken BEHIND it, the
   manager has its turn and writes, and the desk's ev_multi answers `$11`, **A KEY AND A MESSAGE IN ONE WAKE, nothing
   else** — key `$1c0d`, the message in its buffer, the sent mark cleared. Unreachable from any idle; one poll later
   it is the plain outcome. Our build holds there on the host's model and on both blobs. The driver, both shores'
   watch and the host's model take a delivery at such a poll, named by its ordinal (`aes_switch.scheduled(...,
   at_polls=)`).
2. **A press brings the ticks of its click count.** With a double-click wait counted (`gl_bpend` 1) a press opens a
   click count, and the ticks that run it out (`gl_dclick`: 11 on the snapshot's machine) are ticks of every delay
   pending: a 5-tick timer runs out with the menu's press. Measured threshold: a timer of 11 ticks comes, of 12 does
   not. (So EVERY button event wakes a five-tick evnt_timer: the sweep of `evlib.NOT_WOKEN` shows it.)
3. **The menu chain's message is MN_SELECTED byte for byte** (sender 1, title 5, item 30 for View's plain item) **and
   never sets the control manager's "sent" mark** — that mark is the window messages' alone.
4. **ev_mesag's QPB does not outlive the call.** It is the arguments ev_mesag pushed for ap_rdwr; its own Line-F
   return's trap frame overwrites them before the run ends, while the freed EVB still holds their address.
5. **The control manager holds the lock through a press**: it waits for button-up in a loop of yields, so the
   dispatcher never idles there and a release cannot be delivered at an idle of that stretch.
6. **A delay behind others of the same process runs out one delay an idle**: the tick glue counts nothing while a
   run-out countdown waits for tchange to re-arm it.
7. **mwait_act's "arrived" arm is unreachable in a real run** — events are posted by forker, which runs after
   mwait_act in disp; an interrupt only queues a fork. Only the labelled leaf case holds the arm (as band 4 wave 2
   said of it; a real switch does not reach it either).
8. **mn_do over a title left SELECTED and DISABLED, the mouse moved straight off the bar**: the ROM's own run does not
   return within 1.49 M instructions even with clicks delivered. CAUSE NOT INVESTIGATED — recorded, no case.
10. **appl_trecord with a count of 0 — or below — records EVERYTHING.** forker counts the records left down from the
    count and goes on while the result is not 0 (`$fe4ca4 subq.w #1`): from 0 that is −1, and the recorder runs on
    — for 65,536 records by that arithmetic — into a buffer its caller said holds none, until Control-backslash. Only a recording
    ended before its first event records nothing.
11. **A played timer record waits ticks × 100 / scale MILLISECONDS** (lmul, then ldiv, `$fe6666`): a tick is 20 ms, so
    only a scale of 5 plays in real time. At 100 a recorded five-tick wait is 5 ms — no tick, run out by the next
    one; at 1 it is twenty-five ticks; at 3 (166 ms and a remainder) eight; at a negative scale no tick.
12. **A played scale of 0 is the runtime's own zero divide** (ldiv's `divs.w`; vector 5 is an `rte` on this machine):
    the ROM's playback returns. The C refuses by name (above).
13. **A record's NUMBER IS ITS CODE'S LOW WORD** (`tst.w` and three `cmp.w`, `$fe66f8..$fe670a`): `$00050002` is a
    mouse record. **A number that is none of the four is QUEUED AS IT IS**, and forker calls it — a code address in
    an application's data.
14. **ap_trecd's own 100 ms sleeps are the timer records of a recording**: each sleep's five ticks are a tchange
    forker records, merged into the record before while nothing else arrives. **Control going down IS recorded** (a
    key record of data 4, the shift keys changed); **Control and backslash taken in one poll are not**, and end the
    recording.
15. **ap_trecd's compare against tchange decides nothing** (`$fe67ca..$fe6808`): the number is cleared before the four
    compares, so a code that is none of the four is numbered 0 as a timer's is. Dead code in the ROM, kept in the C
    in the ROM's order.
16. **ap_tplay's first act is a yield, and `$c852` / `$c854` (gl_mx, gl_my) are written by it and read by nothing**:
    the playing flag and the mouse's place are stored AFTER the first dsptch, so they hold the mouse where the
    playback FOUND it; no routine of this ROM reads them. And the cursor routine is exchanged BEFORE the motion
    routine, both ways — an order no compared image shows (an interrupt between the two would).
17. **A press HELD on an item of the dropped menu, where the caller is not the message's reader, never idles again**:
    ctlmgr waits for the button to come up IN A LOOP OF YIELDS, the dispatcher has no idle to take the release at
    and the caller never runs — a derivation's whole budget (`aes_evlib.SPINS`; the same press LET GO leaves the
    machine idle, unwoken). Finding 5 from the other side: it is why the sweep's menu chain ends in a click.
18. **The lock the screen manager's menu holds is given up to exactly two chains** — the mouse off the bar and then
    a click, and the menu chain itself (whose click on an item ends the menu too) — and to no interrupt alone.
19. **A parked process that HOLDS the lock waits for whatever it was parked on, and the screen manager's menu waits
    for no key.** Over the lock held by the desk parked for a key (a harness call), a key un-parks the HOLDER; over
    the lock held by the screen manager's menu, the holder is parked with no EVB on its keyboard's wait list
    (`evlib.waits_for_a_key`) — the menu is left by the mouse and a click alone (finding 18).
20. **ap_trecd leaves in D0's high word what its numbering loop last loaded** (`$fe67fc move.l -4(a6),d0`: the
    record's code, a fork function's address — `$00fe`), under its word answer (`$fe6816 move.w d6,d0`); with no
    record numbered the high word is the cursor's distance's (0 under 65,536 bytes). `$00fe0004` after four records.
21. **A RECORDING PAST 32,767 BYTES IS COUNTED BELOW 0, AND NO RECORD OF IT IS NUMBERED.** ap_trecd cuts the
    cursor's distance to a WORD and divides it SIGNED (`$fe67b6 move.w d0,d6 / ext.l d6 / divs.w #8,d6`), then
    numbers under a signed compare (`$fe6812 cmp.w d6,d5 / blt`). A count of 0 records until Control-backslash
    (finding 10), so 4,096 records and more are reached by ROM-run means: 4,110 mouse packets over 137 idles answer
    D0.w = `$f00e` (−4,082) and leave the buffer holding 4,110 fork-function ADDRESSES where an application expects
    numbers — a recording appl_tplay would then queue as code addresses of the ROM (finding 13). "More than 4,095
    records is unreachable" stood in this ledger and in a mutant's equivalence argument until the gate ran it.

**aes — band 5 wave 1, the opcode switch and the marshal (`src/aes/gemsuper.c`): ONE DECLARED DIVERGENCE AWAITING
THE USER'S RULING, what is unpinned, the equivalents, the limits of two guards.**
- **A CONTROL WHOSE int_in COUNT IS ABOVE 20 WORDS, OR addr_in's ABOVE 15 LONGWORDS, IS REFUSED BY NAME ON BOTH BUILDS
  — A DECLARED DIVERGENCE on target, AWAITING THE USER'S RULING.** The marshal's copy in takes its count from the
  program's control and runs past its 62-byte frame over the saved A6 and the return address (`$fe6506..$fe6538`); the
  ROM then `unlk`s into the program's words and RETURNS THROUGH THEM — an address of the program's choosing, in
  supervisor mode (shown on the ROM: `test_the_rom_returns_through_the_program_s_own_words_past_twenty_two`). No C
  has that frame; our build halts (`recreate_not_reconstructed`: `trap #7` on target) BEFORE the copy. A faithful
  version would be hand 68000 for the marshal — unpriced, unscheduled.
- **int_out PAST THE FRAME is reproduced; two things of it are UNPINNED**: a count ABOVE 35 WORDS on target (the copy
  back runs on up the stack as the ROM's does, each build over its own callers' frames — no row: off target the
  host slot models sixteen bytes and refuses beyond them, and on a blob the bench's own entry stack is all that
  lies above), and THE RETURN ADDRESS THROUGH aes_entry (on the bench both shores return to one sentinel, so the
  word is compared; entered through the trap door it is `$fe65bc` in the ROM and OUR aes_entry's address in ours
  — to be mapped through the relocation registry when aes_entry lands).
- **What lies above the frame ON TARGET is GCC's layout, not a contract**: today `link %fp,#-64` with the frame at
  its top, so the saved A6 and the return address follow as in the ROM, then the image pointer before the block's
  address. Held by the blob test of the 35-word row; a compiler that lays the frame elsewhere reds it.
- **The stale int_out words** (an arm that writes fewer answers than the binding asks back): which words a real
  call finds there is its history's. The labelled class stages three and shows the marshal copies back what it
  finds; no ROM run made them.
- **evnt_multi's unset timer local**: the C hands 0 where the ROM hands `-4(a6)` unset. Equivalent while ev_multi
  reads the timer under MU_TIMER alone (it does); not reproduced as a stack read.
- **wm_open of a window already open (or of the desk's; or, over the machine of wind_open's own row, of a handle
  never created) does not return on the ROM** within the oracle's budget: no case of wind_open has one. Not
  investigated further (wm_open is band 3's).
- **THE GUARD "every word an arm reads takes two values" is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT** (the wave's entry): two
  values of a word can be one answer. The sweep is the instrument; the guard keeps a regression to ONE value loud.
- **"A HOOK CALLED WITH NO PASS OPEN" is read in pytest's process and FATAL IN EVERY OTHER** (pass 3: a child ends
  itself by name at the call; a record made before a test is that test's setup error). WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT
  SEE: a hook that is no `AddressHook` (a battery's own ctypes binding — the scheduler model's three, a child's
  per-child door — answers for itself), and a script outside pytest that calls a hook with no pass open now ENDS, by
  name, where it used to be answered 0.
- **THE MARSHAL'S FRAME IS ONE HOST SLOT FOR EVERY PROCESS** (`$7f390`, 78 bytes): wave 3 owes a slot per process.
- **`aes_switch.StackReading` does not follow the switch's table jump**: owed in WAVE 3 (ruling W2-R5), with the first
  path read through the switch — a process that enters the AES by `trap #2`. It is REFUSED BY NAME still, and on no
  path the screen manager's reading reads (`test_aes_stack.py`).
- **The table's relocation guard reads the SHIPPED BLOB's object**: the `atari/` ROM link's own when gemsuper.c joins
  it.
- **The equivalent survivors, accepted** (10 of 751): the kept answer made DONE where the routine answers 1 on every
  path (sh_read, sh_write, sh_get, sh_put, rs_obfix, objc_edit); shel_write's `isover` word at another index or as
  a constant (never read); R_BIPDATA / R_BITBLK in graf_mouse's lookup of a system form.

**aes — band 5 wave 1, slice C (the screen manager's four handlers, `src/aes/gemctrl.c`): ONE DECLARED DIVERGENCE
AWAITING THE USER'S RULING, what is unpinned, what the blobs hold by a pin alone, and what wave 2 inherits.**
- **WM_TOPPED'S WORDS 4..7 — A DECLARED DIVERGENCE an application can see, AWAITING THE USER'S RULING.**
  hctl_window sends `ct_msgup(WM_TOPPED, owner, window, x, y, w, h)` for a press on a window that is not the top one,
  and on that path the ROM never sets x, y, w, h (`$fe489e..$fe48aa` push `-24..-18(a6)`). MEASURED, at seven real
  arrivals of the ROM's own ctlmgr on the low-resolution machine with the two test accessories (the title of the
  other window, another point of it, after a click on the top window's information line, on its title, and three
  more by the review): the ROM sends `$00fe $a85a $0000 $0002` EVERY time — the residue of ctlmgr's preceding
  ev_multi at that depth of the screen manager's stack, the halves of a ROM text address and of a RAM (stack)
  address. OURS SENDS FOUR ZEROS (`HCTL_STALE_WORD`). An application that reads msg[4..7] of WM_TOPPED sees the
  difference. RULED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, pending the user: keep the zeros — the residue is made of code and stack
  addresses a C frame cannot hold by nature, and none is faked. WHY EVERY DIFFERENTIAL IS GREEN: the ROM's routine
  is entered there on the harness's zeroed stack band, where its frame holds zeros too. HELD
  (`test_wm_topped_carries_four_words_of_the_rom_s_stack`): the ROM sends its frame's words (four staged words come
  out, h lowest), and four different real arrivals carry ONE AND THE SAME non-zero residue (the property, not the
  numbers: `$a85a` is a stack address a layout may move). NOT MEASURED: other resolutions, a machine with the desk
  alone (it has no second window), more than two windows, an arrival after a handler that runs deeper than the
  two tried. FOR WAVE 2: once ctlmgr is our C the frame above is GCC's and the residue becomes our build's own —
  the divergence then needs its ruling before it can be measured again.
- **UNPINNED — every mutant of the four handlers that survives both sweeps, with the reason and what was tried:**
  1. THE CALL OF w_bldactive (`$fe45c2`) dropped. W_ACTIVE already holds the top window's gadgets at every arrival
     of every machine made. TRIED: the sweep itself (all cases), and an accessory mode that ANSWERS WM_TOPPED with
     wind_set(WF_TOP) — built, booted and measured, then removed: after the retop the ROM's w_bldactive of the new
     top window changes NOT ONE BYTE of W_ACTIVE (the AES rebuilds it for the new top as it redraws). A stale
     W_ACTIVE needs another window's border drawn after the top one's with no redraw of the top: no call of an
     owner found does that.
  2. gl_mnppd's LOW word read for its HIGH one (`$fe4998 move.w $9730,d7`). The menu's owner is process 0 on every
     machine. WAVE 3 (ruled): an accessory with a menu tree of its own — the test accessory's file would pass its
     one cluster (993 of 1,024 bytes; `accessory_disk.file_at` assumes one).
  3. THE DRAG'S NO-BOUND-BELOW, 10000 (`$fe4682`), made 1000: a 200-line screen cannot tell them apart (the
     mouse's own clamp stops the window first). Unreachable on any machine an ST makes below 1,000 lines.
  4. do_chg's CHECK-DISABLED ARGUMENT made 0 in hctl_rect's AC_OPEN arm (`$fe4974`): it matters only for a
     DISABLED desk title, and no ROM run here disables one (menu_ienable needs the tree's address, which an
     accessory has no call to learn; the desk never disables its first title).
  5. ct_msgup READING THE BUTTON BEFORE ITS SEND instead of after: equal unless the button changes across
     ap_sendmsg, which needs the send to BLOCK or yield (the receiver's pipe full) — every accessory here reads
     its pipe at once. Recorded; a pipe filled by an accessory that never reads is wave 3's kind of machine.
  6. THE TWO CELL MINIMA OF THE SIZER exchanged (gl_wchar / gl_hchar, `$fe4722`, `$fe4728`): a cell is 8 x 8 on
     every machine here (mn_bar's box height has the same hole: no high-resolution machine is derivable).
  7. `<=` for `<` at the elevator's corner: EQUIVALENT, not unpinned — the corner's coordinate is the elevator's
     own, never its track's (shown on the ROM's ob_find along both bars).
  PINNED IN PASS 2, each a review's survivor: each bit of the two gadget masks of the smallest size (three more
  windows, one gadget alone on each bar); the left button ALONE waited up (the right one's packet through the ROM's
  handler); gl_mnclicks counted DOWN, not cleared (two menu_bar calls: 2 → 1); the slider's whole 1000 (the
  elevator dragged past its track's end).
- **ON THE m68k BUILDS THE STATE WHILE PARKED AT A DISPATCH IS HELD BY A CYCLE PIN ALONE.** A blob's run is compared
  where it ENDS (image, answer, registers, ledgers). A handler that scribbles a byte before each yield and heals it
  after (the review's mutant in ct_msgup) leaves the end as it should be: on the blobs it is caught only because
  the rows' whole-run cycles are pinned exactly (126 pin failures, no image failure) — not by any compare of the
  image at the dispatcher. ON THE HOST it is killed AT the dispatcher: the companion compares the image at every
  dispatch of the row's process (by 16 KB page) with the ROM's. So "held by pages" is the host's; the target's
  frame and memory across a yield rest on the pin and on the end. OWED WITH WAVE 2: the image compared at our
  dispatcher's stops on a blob (the watch already stops there), beside the next item.
- **A HANDLER'S FIRST SWITCH BY ITS OWN dsptch IS HELD BY PAGES ON THE HOST, NOT BYTES**: the arrows' yield and
  ct_msgup's (after the lock was let go and the message written — door calls of their own). No road stops a door
  user's child at a dispatcher it reaches OUTSIDE a door call; the companion's image at every dispatch is what
  holds it (a page named). OWED with wave 2, which makes ctlmgr's own dsptch-reaching loop C: a door child halted
  at the hook wherever it is reached, compared byte for byte with the ROM's memory at that dsptch.
- **ctlmgr SPINS WITH NO MENU BAR** (the ROM's, found by an arrival: hctl_rect called again and again after a click
  on the hidden bar's place and a move along it). Pinned as the ROM's behaviour by the arrivals themselves; whether
  a real machine ever leaves the state without the mouse leaving the bar was not run. WAVE 2 reproduces it or says
  why not. AND gl_mnclicks STAYS 1 after two menu_bar calls the screen manager was woken once for: the next real
  click is swallowed (pinned; ctlmgr's and mn_bar's together).
- **THE BLOB SWEEP'S KILLS ARE OF TWO KINDS**: by the second differential's image, or first by a pinned cycle count
  (the sweep stops at a mutant's first failure). A pin moves with any change of the code: such a kill says the row
  ran the changed routine, not that it saw the behaviour — which the host sweep holds.
- **THE DISPATCHER'S-OWN-CALLS RULE MOVED EIGHTEEN PRE-EXISTING ROWS' DERIVATIONS** (`aes_switch._Idling`; the first
  write-up said none): `Scheduled.calls` and `.answers` of aes_ev_multi ×11, aes_ap_tplay ×4, aes_dispatch ×2 and
  aes_ev_block ×1 lose the forker's post_button — rows that ARE a door entry, asleep with no call open, a button
  taken at an idle or a poll of theirs. Harmless: none is a door user (no compare read those lists; the table's
  lines did not move), and the call left out is the forker's post_button and nothing else — held row by row
  (`test_aes_switching.py`, `THE_EIGHTEEN`), every OTHER row's run unchanged by the rule on request (`RUN_SLOW=1`:
  some three hundred ROM runs).

**aes — band 5 wave 1, slices H and G (the leaves round gem_main and the shell): what is unpinned, what waits for a
machine, what the `.S` still names of the ROM, and one rule held for three batteries only.**
- **cart_init's PRESENT arm is UNPINNED by any differential** (`$fed48e..$fed4a2`: the magic `$abcdef42` found at
  `$fa0000`, the cursor left at `$fa0004`, 1 answered). No machine of the oracle's has a cartridge port — the ROM's
  run reads 0 there (ruling R-5: the port is wave 3's, with the loader's cartridge arm, which needs it anyway). Held
  instead: each constant read out of the ROM's own instructions, and the C run ALONE over a host image with the
  magic at the port (`test_aes_cart.py`: "a reading, not a run"). cart_find's rows over a header are a labelled
  ARGUMENT CLASS for the same reason (the cursor staged at a ROM-format header image in RAM).
- **The cart_init twin's ORDER — the cursor stored at the port, then the magic read THROUGH the cursor — has no
  surface.** The ROM's is pinned (its run stopped at the read holds `$fa0000` in `$9ab8`); a twin that read the
  port directly leaves the same image, the same answer and takes no trap (the reviewers' surviving mutant, not
  killed). A surface would be a store ledger read in order; none is built.
- **"Every registered row that switches is held three ways" is a rule for THREE batteries**
  (`test_aes_switching_rows_held.py`: all_run's, the desk's rsrc_free binding's, desk_free's — a row tabled there
  and left out of its premise vet, its blob vet or its table pin reds by name). Read statically it ties 29 of the
  141 rows registered at the time to their three tests; the other batteries parametrise theirs by a scenario's
  key, a wake's name or a session, which no reading of the source ties to a row. THE GENERAL RULE is owed: the three
  vetters (`aes_switching.vet_the_premise`, `vet_on_a_blob`, `vet_the_table_s_price`) noting what they held, and
  `conftest.py` summing it across the workers of a whole-suite run.
- **The vector takes install THE ROM'S handlers on target until wave 3.** `gemdosif.S` is the ROM's bytes, and four
  of its operands are ROM addresses of routines not reconstructed: the AES's `trap #2` handler `$fe3ea6` (sites
  `$fe3c78`, `$fe3c84`) and crit_err `$fe3cbe` (`$fe3c8e`, `$fe3cb6`). Right while the build has no entry for either
  — and `test_aes_rom_data.py::test_a_site_a_transcription_owes_names_a_routine_the_build_has_no_body_of` REDS the
  day it has: the operand then becomes the build's symbol and a `Relocated(ABSOLUTE, …)` of the byte pin, and the
  file's two rows leave the ROM-address census.
- **OWED ON THE PRE-INIT MACHINE** (each routine is verified today over the post-boot machine, a labelled ARGUMENT
  CLASS where the row says so): gem_entry's size_theglo (`$fd9f72`); gem_main's install_trap2 (`$fda074`),
  ini_dlongs, pinit ×3, takeerr (`$fda2bc`) and first sh_tographic (`$fda2c0`); and, after the desk has returned,
  all_run (`$fda396`), giveerr (`$fda39e`) and restore_trap2 (`$fda3d0`) — the last three need a run in which
  deskmain returns (gl_rschange set by app_reschange: the Set Preferences dialog driven).
- **OWED ON THE ACCESSORY MACHINE**: pgmld called by the loader (`$fe433e`) through the ROM's REAL Pexec and Mshrink
  of a real `.ACC` (today every case is over the scripted trap and a staged basepage's three lengths); pinit from
  the accessory allocator; the cartridge pair from the loader's cartridge arm.
- **OWED TO sh_main (wave 4)**: desk_alloc (`$feb1da`) before the desk starts — today five MORE blocks of a TPA
  whose desk still stands — and desk_free (`$feb1e8`) after it returns — today over the running desk's own blocks
  with GEMDOS scripted, so nothing is really given back; the two screen switches round a real launch (`$feb178`,
  `$feb174`); sh_draw's drawing arm over a real launch (`$feb19c`: today the band is drawn over the desk's screen);
  sh_find handed sh_show (`$feb272`, a by-value site no file owes yet); trp14's Getrez.
- **trp14's C twin serves ONE frame** — the function word alone (Getrez) — and halts by name off target over any
  other: the desk's calls through the door (Blitmode's inquiry and the rest) are band 6's, and a C caller that
  pushes more than the word needs the twin widened. The `.S` serves any frame (three shapes held, one made up
  and labelled).
- **Verified and UNPRICED at their own ROM entry, each REGISTERED and in the census**
  (`test_tier3.UNPRICED_AT_A_ROM_ENTRY`): dos_gdrv, dos_chdir and dos_sdrv (a host argument: their caller's return
  site) and, registered by this wave for the same reason, dos_free; takeerr's C twin, pgmld's two C arms under the
  bar and trp14's C twin (each routine ships as its `.S`, whose rows are the table's). OWED, the same class and
  registered nowhere yet: dos_sdta, dos_close and dos_cconout (band 3's batteries).
- **CALL ORDER IS HELD ON THE TWO BLOBS ONLY** (`aes_trap_order`): the host build takes no trap, so a reordering
  that existed in the host build alone would be seen by nothing — there is none to make while both are one C.
- **desk_alloc over a refused FIRST block is REFUSED off target** (`recreate_not_reconstructed`): the ROM does not
  survive it, and the host has no vector page that is taken. On target the C is the ROM's order as it is.
- **The equivalent survivor, accepted** (1 of 165): cart_find's second read of the cursor made through the header
  it has just read — nothing is stored between the two.

**bios — the console's four BLITTER screen routines** (`$fc47be`, `$fc4852`, `$fc48b6`, `$fc4936`): TOS 1.02 installs
them on a machine with a blitter; the captured ST holds the CPU set, and each reconstruction halts on a vector that is
not it. Likewise a console of six or more bit planes — the ROM's own fill table at `$fd15ba` has three entries — and
`$fca914`, the console re-initialisation after a resolution change (still `Setscreen`'s halt; the font-geometry body it `bsr`s into at `$fc4a48` is the escape's v_fontinit, `$fc4a42`, transcribed in band 4).

**bios — `Bconin`'s two remaining drivers are both DEFERRALS, not limits**, and the second half of that is wave 6's own
correction. `Bconin(PRT:)` (`$fc2104`): every chip access is `Giaccess` and its wait is a declared GPIP list away (it
waits for BUSY to be ASSERTED). `Bconin(AUX:)` (`$fc2150`) was recorded as needing an interrupt to fill the RS232 input
ring; it does not. Its body is `lea $c54,a0 / bsr $fc2892` — the same blocking ring reader `rs232_ring_get` already is,
on the input ring instead of the output one, which a case STAGES exactly as `test_bios_bconin.py` stages the console's —
and then a flow-control tail: the mode byte at `32(a0)`, a low-water compare against `10(a0)`, and either a direct
`$ff8800` read-modify-write dropping RTS (`psg_seed` serves it) or an XON planted at `33(a0)` and the MFP TSR test and
transmitter prime THIS WAVE RECONSTRUCTED for `Bconout(AUX:)` (a declared `$fffa2d` serves that). What is missing is the
cases and one parameter — `rs232_ring_get` names `IOREC_RS232_OUT` where the ROM takes its ring in A0.

**bios — honest gaps in the console.** WHICH `b??` `cell_address`'s two clamps are is now HALF DRIVEN. Wave 6's review
found them transcribed as signed compares where the ROM's `cmp.w / bpl` tests the N FLAG OF THE WORD DIFFERENCE — two
different functions once that subtraction overflows — and `test_bios_vt52.py` drives the difference at the overflow
window (a column of `$8000` and `$8027` clamp; `$8028` does not), so `bpl` against `blt` is pinned and
`advance_cursor`'s own `blt` is pinned by being the other answer. What is still read off the disassembly and not driven
is `bpl` against a `bcc` for the COLUMN: it would take a coordinate whose unclamped cell address is not in the machine's
megabyte even wrapped, so the reconstruction's own bound fires where the original walks its address space. The ROW's is driven
since band 4 (an ESC Y row byte below the bias, which the console now wraps on the 24-bit bus as the ROM does). And
the console's poison/attribution pass is OFF: the bytes the oracle writes ARE the driver's control state, so poison
would be indistinguishable from the routine's own output; `vt52.canary` stands in for the pixel cases.

**bios — the floppy VBL** (`$fc1bc4`, reached from `isr_vbl` past the `flock` gate) stays halted on the PSG's account:
it merges drive-select bits with a direct YM2149 read-modify-write, a path this project has no door for (see wave 5).

**gemdos — the dispatcher's arms are RECONSTRUCTED as of fs wave 3 band 4; what is not is everything behind the
termination record's longjmp.** The REDIRECTED arms (`$fd328a`), the DEVICE arm (`$fc99bc`) and the DEVICE-NAME arm
(`$fc9aca`) are verified, and the media-change recovery's two helpers `$fc93f4`/`$fc9468` are proved STANDALONE. What is
NOT: the E_CHG RECOVERY `$fc951e..$fc973a` (the drive's OFDs, the FAT OFD, node slots, DND tree and DMD freed, `Getbpb`,
`$fc53c0`, re-dispatch at `$fc94ee`) and the non-E_CHG error arm `$fc96e8` — both are reached through a `longjmp` over a
record the C core does not have, and a host longjmp cannot unwind through the ctypes frames of the handler hook. A future
caller of `gemdos_free_drive_ofds` must pass whatever A4 the innermost fs routine left, NOT the DMD, or it silently fixes the
ROM's bug. Two DIVERGENCES are recorded, not pinned: the redirected `Cconin` at EOF answers the stale `-14(a6)` byte (pinned
off target only; on target it is an uninitialised C local), and after an echoing redirected `Cconrs` the ROM's `$7ef4`
record points into a dead nested frame while the C leaves it untouched (the cases drop that span from the compare by name,
since VDI band 3 as a `case.run(dropped_windows=…)` window — a slice that never nests leaves it unwritten and compared — and the
Tier 3 row carries the same named mask). The
PROCESS-TERMINATION RECORD at `$7ef4` is omitted
rather than halted, because the ROM arms it before any reconstructed arm and a halt would stop every case: it is the
68000 frame of the `jsr` that armed it, which a C core has no counterpart for, and `test_gemdos_dispatch.py` measures
the hole at exactly twelve bytes. ON TARGET THE OMISSION HAS A CONSEQUENCE, and it is worth writing down before
anything depends on it: a ROM built from these cores would leave `$7ef4` holding whatever last wrote it, so the FILE
SYSTEM's critical-error abort (`$fc5986` and four more, through the `longjmp` at `$fc4f54`) would jump through a stale
record — and so would `Pexec`, which saves the outer record and arms its own. It is NOT `Pterm`: wave 7 said so and
wave 2 of this component disproved it — `Pterm` `jsr`s into the trap entry's epilogue at `$fc4fe8` and touches the
record not at all (`$fc8028`'s row). Nothing compiles these cores into a ROM yet — the bench blob enters the
dispatcher as a C function and never terminates a process — so nothing is broken by it today, and nothing pins it
either. The surface that would is a Tier 2 row over a call that aborts.

**gemdos — `Tsetdate`/`Tsettime` are verified on their REJECTING arms only.** Both end in XBIOS `Settime`
(`$fc50b4`, a `trap #14` that writes the 6301's clock over the IKBD ACIA), which is not reconstructed. Every bound the
two routines apply is in reach — and two of them turn out to apply to nothing at all: the year bound and the hour bound
are DEAD CODE in TOS 1.02, both through a sign extension, and both are reproduced with a case.

**gemdos — the PROCESS group's one modelling limit (it has no halts left).** `Fclose` of an open FILE is reconstructed
(fs wave 3 band 2), the dispatcher's character-device routing (band 4), and `Pexec` modes 0 and 3 LOAD (band 4:
`$fc6d14` looks the file up, `$fc85ea` loads and relocates it). The limit is the Mega ST battery
clock: the probe at `$fc4c0c` WRITES two registers and READS THEM BACK, and the kit's declared I/O map has exactly two
forms for such an address — a CONSTANT, which a store makes stale, and WRITE-THROUGH, which is what a chip that is
really there does. So every case in this group declares a machine WITH the clock fitted, and the `bcs` at `$fc5096`
that makes `gemdos_resync_clock` a no-op on a plain ST — the arm this snapshot's own machine takes — is driven by an
ORACLE claim and recorded unpinned. The kit door that would close it is a THIRD column beside
`OS_IO_DECLARED_CONSTANT`/`OS_IO_WRITE_THROUGH`: "a register a store does not reach". The RP5C15's registers are BANKED
(the probe writes in mode 9 and the digits are read in mode 8), so under a one-value-per-address map three of the
thirteen digits read back the probe's own bytes — `gemdos_process.served()` is what the cases compute their
expectations from.

**gemdos — `Pexec`'s save of the OUTER termination record has no differential, so it has TWO half-cases.** `$fc81c2`
copies the twelve bytes at `$7ef4` to `$7560` and `$fc81e0` immediately arms a new one, which is the hole
`test_gemdos_dispatch.py` measures — so nothing can span the copy. The ORACLE's half is
`test_pexec_saves_the_dispatcher_s_own_termination_record_before_it_arms_one` (stopped at the arming); the
CANDIDATE's is `test_our_pexec_copies_that_record_too`, which had to STAGE a distinctive record at `$7ef4` and a
fill at `$7560` to say anything at all — the captured machine's `$7560` already holds a byte-for-byte copy of its
own `$7ef4`, and against the snapshot alone a run that copied NOTHING read exactly like one that copied correctly
(measured: deleting the loop left the first spelling of that case green).

**gemdos — `Pterm`'s exit code in D0 at the epilogue is pinned by construction and by no surface.** On target the
epilogue's first instruction (`$fc4fee`, `move.l d0,$68(a5)`) re-stores D0 over the slot `Pterm` has just written,
and the ROM arrives there with the exit code in D0 (`$fc806c`). The reconstruction pins D0 as an input of its
`jsr gemdos_trap1_epilogue` (`src/gemdos/process.c`); unpinned, every parent on target would resume with whatever
the release loops last left there. NOTHING SEES IT: the host build returns instead of jumping, and the checkpoint
cases stop the ORIGINAL at its own `jsr`, so neither shore executes the epilogue. The surface that would catch it
is a BENCH TRANSCRIPTION case — both sides entered at a staged caller with the parent's `+$7c` frame pointing at a
stub, compared at the `rte` — and it is PARKED below rather than written, because the transcription bench enters at
a caller and a `Pterm` case would have to stage a whole second process's saved frame for it.

**gemdos — the file system's five BIOS-error arms are ONE reason in five places.** Every disk call in
`src/gemdos/fs_disk.c` ends the same way: store the result at `$75b4`, and if it is non-zero record the drive at
`$87cc` and longjmp through the process-termination record at `$7ef4` (`$fc4f54`). That record is the dispatcher's own
omission — the 68000 frame of the `jsr` that armed it — so the error arm halts on both builds and the success arm,
which is every arm a working disk takes, is reconstructed whole. The `$75b4` store is NOT part of the halt: the ROM
makes it unconditionally and so does this. `Mediach` answering 2 (a definite media change) is the same halt reached
from the other side. Two EQUIVALENT MUTANTS are recorded rather than pinned: `Mediach` asked with the DMD's `m_drvnum`
instead of the buffer's `b_bufdrv` (the hit test has just proved them equal), and `$fc50ca`'s signed compares written
unsigned. And `$fc5a98` on an EMPTY list is transcribed but unreached: the ROM reads the link of BCB 0 — the reset
vector — and would `Rwabs` through whatever `image[16..19]` holds. The DMD is a STAGED INPUT computed by the ROM's own
expressions — and since wave 9 a CHECKED one: `$fc53c0` is reconstructed and `test_gemdos_fs_drive.py` requires the
ROM's builder, run over the staged BPB, to produce the staged records byte for byte; `hdv_bpb` is exercised by `$fc67de`.

**gemdos — what a routine that reaches the BIOS still owes the harness.** Every GEMDOS call into the BIOS goes through
`gemdos_bios_trampoline` ($fc4eac): the oracle takes a real `trap #13`, whose dispatcher parks a return address at
`$eb0` and frames 46 bytes below `savptr`. The TARGET build takes the same trap, so nothing is owed there. The HOST
build cannot — there is no 68000 — and calls the BIOS core directly, which leaves two residuals: the parked longword,
which the reconstruction therefore stores itself from a named constant per call site, and the register frame, which is
neither excluded nor ignored but DECLARED — `test/gemdos.py`'s `machine()` pokes `savptr` into the run's own stack
band, so the frame lands where the differential already drops bytes and every other byte is compared as usual.
`harness._vet_exclude_bands` would refuse an exclusion here (neither band is stack, correctly), which is why the
declaration is the shape rather than a band.

**gemdos — the character devices' three halts.** `^C` in the typeahead poll ends the process through `Pterm`
(`$fc8028`, reconstructed in GEMDOS wave 2 but a CHECKPOINT case — it does not return, so a console leaf that
tail-called it would have no `rts` for its own differential either); a standard handle outside -3..-1 is refused by `console.c`'s own `per_device`,
because the ROM's six per-device tables are sized for exactly three entries in straight-line code and a fourth
indexes off all of them (it is not the dispatcher's handle-resolution arm — that one is for a handle ABOVE 0, which
the dispatcher redirects before a leaf ever sees it); and `Cauxin` inherits `Bconin(AUX:)` (`$fc2150`), which
`src/bios/bcon.c` defers for want of a staged input ring. Each halts on both builds rather than answering something
plausible.

**gemdos — the dispatcher's pop count is UNPINNED.** `call_handler`'s target build keeps the number of bytes to unwind
in D3 across the `jsr` into the handler, because D2 — where it used to sit — is scratch that a real GEMDOS leaf writes:
`Cauxout` reaches `xconout_rs232`'s `move.b $fffc00,d2`, and so do `Cprnout` and a `Cconout` of BEL. Off target the
handler is a host hook and writes no 68000 register, so no differential can see the difference; on the bench blob it
would, but every dispatcher row registered so far names a handler whose whole body is a `moveq`. Putting the count back
in D2 was measured to leave `make test`, `make guarded` and `make bench` green (only the dispatcher's own Tier 3 ratio
moves, and that is a cost pin rather than a correctness one). THE ROW THAT WOULD PIN IT is a dispatcher-SLICE case on a
character-device selector, which needs the console group's staged machine under a slice case — not written.

**gemdos — the memory manager's two honest gaps, neither of them a halt.** ONE SURVIVING MUTANT: the null guard on the
forward merge in `gemdos_md_free_insert`. No pool this harness can produce reaches it — it would take a free list whose
successor link is NULL where the list is not empty — so it is recorded unpinned rather than pinned by a fabricated
record. And the ALCYON OUTGOING-ARGUMENT SLOT: every routine in this group saves one register more than it restores
(D5/D6/D7), because Alcyon reserves the four-byte slot a callee's first argument is written into by pushing one, and
the epilogue drops it with `tst.l (sp)+`. What the arguments overwrite is that STACK SLOT and not the register — no
body here writes the register itself, which the verifier checked over all of them — so a caller's copy survives and
there is nothing for a differential to see either way.
Both ROM DEFECTS the group found are reproduced rather than corrected, with a case each: `Mshrink` writing through NULL
into the reset vectors on a spent pool, and the SIGNED grow check that lets `$80000000` past.
